ar: تستلم الخدمة المستضافة الصوت العربي لتفريغه؛ ويتلقى Codex النص والبيانات الوصفية اللازمة للمراجعة وإعداد مخرجات بلغة الحالة المختارة.

بالنسبة إلى تسجيل موجود، تستلم الخدمة ملف الصوت والبيانات الوصفية المقدمة، مثل العنوان والتاريخ والمشاركين والمحاور ولغة التسجيل. وعند بدء تسجيل موثّق من حالة، تستلم أيضاً سياقاً موجزاً مشتقاً من `case_brief.md` داخل جسم طلب HTTPS وليس داخل عنوان URL؛ ولا يرفق المسار البديل الصريح غير الموثّق هذا الملخص. ينتج النموذج المستضاف النص العربي، لكنه لا يملك القرار النهائي في إسناد المتحدثين.

لأغراض الإسناد والمراجعة، قد يقرأ Codex النص العربي الخام والبيانات الوصفية للمصدر والملاحظات المفيدة وقائمة المتحدثين المعروفين والنسخة المنسوبة. يُحفظ النص العربي الأصلي غير المنسوب، وتقتصر التصحيحات على أخطاء التفريغ الواضحة. تبقى ملفات الصوت والحزم والنصوص في الملفات المحلية بعد الاستيراد؛ ويتطلب استخدامها في ورقة عمل أو مخرج باللغة الإنجليزية خطوة منفصلة ومسجلة.
de: Der gehostete Dienst erhält das zu transkribierende Audio; Codex erhält Transkript und Metadaten für die Prüfung.

Bei einer bestehenden Aufnahme erhält der Dienst die Audiodatei und bereitgestellte Metadaten wie Titel, Datum, Teilnehmer, Interviewer und Sprache. Bei authentifizierter Aufnahme aus einer Akte erhält er zusätzlich kompakten Kontext aus `case_brief.md` im HTTPS-Anfragekörper, nie in der URL; der ausdrückliche Fallback ohne Authentifizierung fügt dieses Briefing nicht bei. Das gehostete Modell erzeugt das Transkript, entscheidet aber nicht endgültig über Sprecherzuordnungen.

Für Zuordnung und Prüfung kann Codex Rohtranskript, Quellenmetadaten, hilfreiche Notizen, bekannte Sprecher und zugeordnete Fassung lesen. Das ursprüngliche nicht zugeordnete Transkript bleibt erhalten; Korrekturen beschränken sich auf eindeutige Transkriptionsfehler. Audio, Bundles und Transkripte bleiben nach dem Import in lokalen Dateien; ihre Nutzung im Workpaper oder Deliverable erfordert einen getrennten, protokollierten Schritt.
en: The hosted service receives the audio to transcribe; Codex receives the transcript and metadata needed for review.

For an existing recording, the service receives the audio file and supplied metadata such as title, date, participants, interviewer, and language. For authenticated capture launched from a case, it also receives compact context derived from `case_brief.md` in the HTTPS request body, never in the URL; the explicit unauthenticated fallback does not attach that brief. The hosted model produces the transcript but is not the final speaker-attribution authority.

For attribution and review, Codex may read the raw transcript, source metadata, useful notes, known-speaker list, and attributed version. The original unattributed transcript is preserved, and corrections are limited to clear transcription errors. Audio, bundles, and transcripts remain in local files after import; using them in the workpaper or a deliverable requires a separate, recorded step.
es: El servicio alojado recibe el audio que debe transcribir; Codex recibe la transcripción y los metadatos necesarios para revisarla.

Para una grabación existente, el servicio recibe el archivo de audio y los metadatos aportados, como título, fecha, participantes, entrevistador e idioma. Para una captura autenticada iniciada desde un expediente, también recibe contexto compacto derivado de `case_brief.md` en el cuerpo HTTPS, nunca en la URL; el modo alternativo explícito sin autenticación no adjunta ese brief. El modelo alojado produce la transcripción, pero no es la autoridad final para atribuir hablantes.

Para la atribución y revisión, Codex puede leer la transcripción sin tratar, metadatos de origen, notas útiles, lista de hablantes conocidos y versión atribuida. Se conserva el original sin atribuir y las correcciones se limitan a errores evidentes. Audio, paquetes y transcripciones permanecen en archivos locales tras la importación; usarlos en el papel de trabajo o en un entregable requiere un paso separado y registrado.
fr: Le service hébergé reçoit l'audio à transcrire ; Codex reçoit la transcription et les métadonnées nécessaires à la revue.

Pour un enregistrement existant, le service reçoit le fichier audio et les métadonnées fournies, telles que titre, date, participants, interviewer et langue. Pour une capture authentifiée lancée depuis un dossier, il reçoit aussi un contexte compact issu de `case_brief.md` dans le corps HTTPS, jamais dans l'URL ; le fallback explicite sans authentification n'attache pas ce brief. Le modèle hébergé produit la transcription mais n'est pas l'autorité finale d'attribution des locuteurs.

Pour l'attribution et la revue, Codex peut lire transcription brute, métadonnées source, notes utiles, liste des locuteurs connus et version attribuée. L'original non attribué est conservé et les corrections se limitent aux erreurs de transcription évidentes. Audio, bundles et transcriptions restent dans les fichiers locaux après import ; leur utilisation dans le workpaper ou un livrable exige une étape séparée et tracée.
it: Il servizio ospitato riceve l'audio da trascrivere; Codex riceve trascrizione e metadati necessari alla revisione.

Per una registrazione esistente, il servizio riceve il file audio e i metadati forniti, come titolo, data, partecipanti, intervistatore e lingua. Per una cattura avviata da un fascicolo autenticato riceve anche un contesto compatto ricavato da `case_brief.md` nel corpo HTTPS, mai nell'URL; il fallback senza autenticazione esplicita non allega quel brief. Il modello ospitato produce la trascrizione ma non decide l'attribuzione finale dei parlanti.

Per attribuzione e revisione, Codex può leggere trascrizione grezza, metadati sorgente, note utili, elenco dei parlanti noti e versione attribuita. L'originale non attribuito viene conservato e le correzioni devono limitarsi a errori evidenti. Audio, bundle e trascrizioni restano nei file locali dopo l'importazione; l'inserimento nel workpaper o in un deliverable richiede un passaggio separato e tracciato.

Enabled OCR remains enabled across later core updates. Package-index request-log retention is controlled by the configured index. Failed updates invalidate the readiness receipt and require repair before execution; this shared environment has no retained generations.

external_boundaries.content: Random installation UUID and opaque capability, Vera/host/runtime versions, platform and workflow technical IDs, failed stage, complete available technical diagnostic chains and measurements, explicit missing-measurement reasons, retry IDs and actual recovery outcomes. No professional helper stdout, client documents, case text, user prompts or arbitrary task logs. Known path, email and credential patterns are removed from technical messages; this mechanical filter does not establish semantic privacy. The host agent must select technical evidence without unrelated personal/client material. The remote channel does not read local files. Failed helpers retain complete stderr privately on disk; stderr may include unrelated private/client text and is read by the selected host model for semantic review under its existing account. Raw stderr is not forwarded to Mparanza. Only reviewed relevant technical diagnostics, linked by the original report UUID, are submitted as supplemental evidence. Professional stdout is not captured. Managed helpers also send source-bound exception classes, OS error numbers, package-relative stack coordinates, developer-authored error templates and missing required option names automatically. Dynamic exception/argument values, locals, professional stdout and arbitrary source excerpts are not part of these structured events. Process-session UUIDs, persistent operation UUIDs and optional keyed digests of existing run/input-receipt identities bind attempts without disclosing receipt fields or raw client-input hashes. Actual worker interpreter/platform fields are separate from the reporter's interpreter. Capture completeness, pending semantic review, exact remedy/retry events and host verification of the original task remain distinct evidence states; a structured event is not a semantic diagnosis.
controls: Only closed technical transport schemas are accepted; unknown fields and arbitrary recovery commands are rejected.
The fixed HTTPS transport refuses redirects. Reporting failures retain the outbox and do not discard professional outputs.
The remote connector is independent of local command-process startup. If the host cannot expose/connect it, no successful report is claimed.
Only two built-in setup/preparation retries may execute automatically, once per remedy revision. Client documents, ACLs and security settings are not changed.
A published update is not recovery. The failed operation must actually execute successfully before that installation delivery closes.

Supplemental diagnostics require ownership of the original report and matching execution metadata; they are stored separately and cannot change the original report UUID, delivery status or remedy revision. Raw local diagnostic files can only be removed by acknowledging a matching recorded supplement.
Actionable remedies target an explicit original report. Each delivery uses its own applicable revision; a different report with the same generic signal does not inherit that remedy.

A cached actual connector status permits only the two fixed retries for an existing matching local receipt and latest report. It performs no direct HTTP polling or identity adoption. Missing local receipts cannot be fabricated to authorise a retry.

A helper success records readiness. Host AI verification of the original task and inputs is required for all recovered outcomes, including setup/startup. Delayed failures cannot reopen an already recovered episode.
Failed fixed retries retain complete stderr privately for semantic review. Raw recovery stderr is not automatically transmitted.

An explicitly selected MPARANZA_INCIDENT_DELIVERY=local-only setting blocks automatic client HTTP transport for this execution while preserving local evidence. Incident queues are durably marked and not automatically flushed later; this does not make model-provider processing local-only.
external_boundaries.destination: Mparanza HTTPS operational-incident API and Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint
external_boundaries.purpose: Diagnose observed execution/setup failures, return installation-specific remedies and receive actual recovery outcomes
external_boundaries.retention: Local capability, pending reports and receipts persist outside client folders. The service retains incident, report, remedy and outcome records; no automatic deletion period is enforced. Status access is scoped by the opaque capability. Pending diagnostic pointers and raw stderr persist in the private incident directory until a matching actual recorded supplementation receipt is acknowledged; unsuccessful review or delivery retains them. Supplementation never replaces the original recovery episode or reopens recovered records. Recorded original/outcome receipts can acknowledge only their exact local queued UUID without replacing the local capability or saved connector identity. Remedy revisions are retained from the surviving migration revision onward; overwritten legacy revisions are not reconstructed.

security_controls.control: Setup validates package-relative selections and installs the published shared recipe. No package names or dependency instructions are accepted from client documents.
security_controls.on_violation: An unknown module, missing requirements file, invalid target, or failed dependency validation stops the helper instead of executing it in a partial environment.

security_controls.control: One fixed environment is located outside plugin source and client folders. An exclusive operating-system installation lock waits for running managed Python readers, which hold a shared lease through a startup hook. Setup removes the ready receipt before mutation and restores it only after pip check and component validation. Failed setup leaves execution unavailable until repair. Symlink roots, locks and metadata are rejected. The installer is launched from base Python to avoid self-deadlock. This lease is concurrency protection, not a security sandbox. Other historical environments are not automatically deleted. State metadata normally uses atomic replacement. Only EXDEV or Windows error 17 falls back under the same installer lock to a single-link regular-file write with full-byte writes and fsync. Failed writes attempt to restore existing metadata or remove a newly created file; the ready receipt remains invalid until setup succeeds. This fallback is local and does not add a recipient or payload.
security_controls.on_violation: A target creation or validation failure returns a bounded setup error and the requested helper is not run.

security_controls.control: For the six explicitly supported assured modules, the launchers verify the complete package inventory and stable regular-file bytes against the embedded build-generated SHA-256 index. Symlinks, reparse entries, special files, extra directories/files, missing or changed code and unstable reads stop preparation. Unchanged hardlinked package code is materialized into a fresh private OS temporary directory; each copied file is re-read and must have one physical link, then the unchanged component integrity validator must pass. The managed installation and aliases are not modified. The copy contains indexed product code/assets, not client documents, credentials, workflow reports or dependency environments. This local index detects package drift; it is not a publisher signature, a signed origin attestation or proof of installed-host acceptance. Successful code copies remain in OS temporary storage for normal OS cleanup. The root-level host .in_use directory is non-executable bookkeeping: only ASCII numeric, ordinary single-link regular marker files are excluded from the product inventory. Nested directories, links, reparse points and non-numeric names there are rejected. Marker contents are not read, executed, transmitted or included in a recovery copy; host markers and installed product files are not modified.
security_controls.on_violation: Preparation failures and host permission denials stop execution. A failed private copy is removed; no installation chmod/unlink/manual repair, alternate sandbox or relaxed component validation is permitted.

security_controls.control: The parent Vera launcher reports a negative exit code or 137/247 as forced termination. It writes execution_failure.json only inside the selected workflow context output directory or its normalization/sample subdirectories; without that matching context it logs only. The diagnostic stores workflow/run identifiers, exit status and an explicit statement that memory exhaustion is not established by the exit code. It makes no model calls or network requests.
security_controls.on_violation: A worker failure remains failure; diagnostic persistence errors are logged rather than converted into a success.

security_controls.control: The standalone Python bootstrap passes uv only declared host paths, locale, proxy, CA and cache settings, preserving original environment-name casing. Unrelated token/API-key variables and inherited UV_*, VIRTUAL_ENV, CONDA_PREFIX, PYTHONHOME and PYTHONPATH are excluded; private UV_PYTHON_* and UV_CACHE_DIR values are set by the bootstrap. The same environment is used for interpreter discovery and its local probe.
security_controls.on_violation: Undeclared environment names are absent from every bootstrap child process.

security_controls.control: The built-in incident dependency-setup retry uses the shared host/runtime environment allowlist, named runtime/state locations and recovery recursion guard instead of inheriting unrelated user tokens and keys.
security_controls.on_violation: Undeclared environment names are absent from the child environment.

security_controls.control: When the maintained launcher itself runs under Python -I -B, it restores only its own resolved scripts directory for sibling technical-diagnostic imports. It does not add the caller working directory. Helper execution, diagnostic retention and explicit incident delivery policy remain unchanged.
security_controls.on_violation: The maintained launcher must stop rather than resolving technical diagnostics from the caller working directory.

external_boundaries.content: Random installation UUID and opaque capability, Clara/host/runtime versions, platform and workflow technical IDs, failed stage, complete available technical diagnostic chains and measurements, explicit missing-measurement reasons, retry IDs and actual recovery outcomes. No professional helper stdout, client documents, case text, user prompts or arbitrary task logs. Known path, email and credential patterns are removed from technical messages; this mechanical filter does not establish semantic privacy. The host agent must select technical evidence without unrelated personal/client material. The remote channel does not read local files. Saved anonymous connector authorization exchanges a random code with a PKCE verifier, client ID and fixed incident resource; the host saves access/refresh tokens. The server stores token/code hashes, technical callback metadata and a random connection UUID. No personal account signup, user profile, email or client-file permission is involved. Failed helpers retain complete stderr privately on disk; stderr may include unrelated private/client text and is read by the selected host model for semantic review under its existing account. Raw stderr is not forwarded to Mparanza. Only reviewed relevant technical diagnostics, linked by the original report UUID, are submitted as supplemental evidence. Professional stdout is not captured. Installation-preparation failures submit only a fixed technical message, exception type/errno, or the indexed package-relative file name and expected/observed SHA-256 values for a content mismatch. No altered file contents or professional files are read for this report. Managed helpers also send source-bound exception classes, OS error numbers, package-relative stack coordinates, developer-authored error templates and missing required option names automatically. Dynamic exception/argument values, locals, professional stdout and arbitrary source excerpts are not part of these structured events. Process-session UUIDs, persistent operation UUIDs and optional keyed digests of existing run/input-receipt identities bind attempts without disclosing receipt fields or raw client-input hashes. Actual worker interpreter/platform fields are separate from the reporter's interpreter. Capture completeness, pending semantic review, exact remedy/retry events and host verification of the original task remain distinct evidence states; a structured event is not a semantic diagnosis. Current reporting-process version, protocol capabilities and server last-seen time are retained per process session, separately from historical failure versions; they do not establish that all conversations updated. Native-host binding, when invoked, accepts a random host UUID and scoped capability plus an optional explicit native-app label at the same incident service. Only the host capability hash is retained server-side. Stable app-profile UUIDs are derived from host UUID and app label; reporter-instance UUIDs may be task-local and do not count physical computers, plugin copies or people. App grouping grants no additional client status or outcome access. Operator views retain each original report, supplement, outcome and retry event with its actual reporting owner and server receipt time; missing historical task identity is not reconstructed. The native stdio identity bridge verifies its indexed entry, reporter, technical collector and product metadata, then executes an isolated temporary reporter snapshot using existing Python without installing dependencies. Its tool accepts only an existing reporter capability and sends host proof to the fixed register endpoint; it never returns the device key or copies the reporter key into the host identity file. Native broker version/session observations are retained separately from guest reporter and failure-worker observations. When native tools are not exposed in cloud Cowork, the saved remote connector continues to report under its distinct connection identity and physical-host linkage remains unknown; no device controls or folder permissions are expanded automatically. Native-helper failures return source-bound exception classes, errno or HTTP status, package-relative frames and developer-authored templates. Dynamic diagnostic values are not returned; unavailable capture is explicit. This bridge does not return raw stderr or device keys. The central recovery agent may request named technical evidence surfaces through a diagnostic-request remedy. The host AI replies with reviewed technical facts, the original report UUID and request revision. Original-task availability is represented by technical booleans, not task text, client identifiers or file contents. A resume remedy communicates a diagnosed correction to the existing authorized workflow; it does not carry executable code. Technical requests, response UUIDs, applicable revisions and their observed status are retained with the original episode. The central agent may implement and deploy incident-related software fixes through reviewed source and green CI under Fabio’s explicit recovery authorization; it does not receive professional case files or gain user-host permissions. Handled Studio Archive exceptions log their active traceback locally before returning the existing error JSON, allowing the same source-bound collector and host semantic review to retain their actual cause. The operator derives diagnostic publication, exact owner/report/revision receipt and reply states, the existing 15-minute deadline and reporting-owner last service contact from retained records. These delivery facts do not establish physical-host availability, diagnosis or original-task recovery. The operator also projects exact delivery, retry and original-task outcome evidence for all actionable remedy kinds, including software updates. Its 15-minute attention cadence is not an execution timeout. A local alert renderer uses technical incident facts and an AI-reviewed blocker, accountable next action, reason and scheduled check. An optional operator-maintained device label is accepted only with a recorded exact-device verification reference; it is not inferred from the recipient, OS or reporter identity. Rendered operator alerts may include opaque machine/case codes and a verified operator-device label, but no client contents, raw diagnostics, personal identifiers or credentials. The renderer neither sends email nor accesses the registry or client files. It rejects stale followup reviews and cannot assign an unreceived or overdue remedy back to the uncontacted Clara. Recovered labels require matching actual original-task success evidence; incomplete historical bindings remain unknown. The shared API also exposes a separate public workflow-testing endpoint: an allowlisted map of pipeline IDs to testing levels and baseline metadata, without incident details, computer IDs, run IDs or user feedback. Its reset is operator-only and does not change incident records. Native workflow transport supplies the same existing host proof during registration when it is available. The shared managed launcher also reports handled PDF recovery failures and subsequent attempts for journal-sampling and journal-bank-reconciliation. It projects fixed strategy/check identifiers, pass/fail/replay flags and attempt/readable-row counts only; PDF text, amounts, paths, adapter code and free-text rationale remain local. Supplements reuse the original report identity across process sessions and cannot certify original-task recovery. Other products carry the shared implementation but do not expose these journal workflows. Bank PDF inspection failures and subsequent corrections are linked per source, independently of journal failures. The bank source digest used in the episode key stays in local reporting state and is not added to transmitted evidence. Other bank statements cannot inherit that extraction recovery.

PDF recovery evidence uses the existing durable outbox and exact original-report supplementation, including local-only delivery. Readable partial results and independent workflow gates survive incident-service failure. Frozen extraction is explicitly unqualified and never generates a recovered outcome.

external_boundaries.content: Unless the user requests --local-only, each substantive run with a durable local report automatically sends exactly schema version, one random per-run receipt UUID, the Clara version when the request was first created, and the SHA-256 digest of the canonical local model-data report, plus ordinary connection metadata. The report itself, workflow and local run IDs, client or case data, professional purpose, phase labels, counts, filenames, file contents, source-document hashes, prompts, and model outputs are not sent. A later verification request sends the same opaque receipt UUID and report digest. Clara and Lucia use receipt schema 2 with the explicit product as a fifth signed request field; legacy Vera schema 1 is preserved.
controls: Vera report builds stamp by default. When the user prohibits external receipt transmission, --local-only writes the local JSON and readable report, returns not_requested/local_only, and skips receipt request construction and transport. It does not change host model processing. Do not retry stamping without a later explicit user request. Service failures leave completed work and the local report intact and return pending. The generic Studio Archive helper also disables server attestation.

The client constructs a four-field allow-listed request, restricts production traffic to the fixed Mparanza HTTPS route, permits HTTP only on an explicit loopback port for testing, bounds responses, and rejects additional or mismatched response fields. The default transport rejects HTTP redirects before any redirected request and rejects endpoint URLs containing credentials.

The server rejects additional request fields, assigns its own timestamp, signs the complete retained record with Ed25519, stores only the minimal proof fields, applies request-size and rate limits, and fails closed when signing or verification keys are unavailable.

The local customer receipt states that the proof covers existence, server time, and report integrity only; it does not claim who submitted the digest, provider delivery, analytical correctness, semantic necessity, DPIA completion, legal advice, or GDPR compliance.

Retries retain the original UUID and version. A retry after finalization verifies the retained report against the sealed artifact manifest and writes supplementary receipts outside the immutable output tree.

The workflow remains subject to host network permissions and action-specific approval rules. A denied transmission is not retried through another tool or destination; permission-denied retries wait for the required authorization.

OpenAI desktop onboarding is a local-only exception: reports beneath its .vera-onboarding-local-only directory marker return not_requested/local_onboarding before receipt request construction, including direct later stamp retries. The Claude projection omits this new onboarding behavior.

The report build returns the readable local report as display_markdown for the final response, including when stamping is pending. The show command renders a saved report after validating its recorded hashes; it reads no source documents, writes no files and makes no network or stamping request. Displaying the report uses the current model context and does not send its content to Mparanza.

The separately registered workflow-usage service can link the retained receipt UUID and digest to the installation and primary task. It does not alter the four-field stamping request or send the report itself. See workflow-usage for outcome and optional star/comment fields.

The shared implementation binds registrations, OAuth resources, task events, report signatures, feedback and update downloads to one product. Existing unmapped installations and receipt schema 1 remain Vera. Physical-computer identity is shared, while usage catalogues and testing epochs are separated by product.

The workflow-usage connector can relay the same retained allow-listed stamping request when local HTTPS is unavailable. Its surrounding envelope includes the existing workflow run UUID and original reporter credentials for ownership checks; the proof service retains only the original proof fields. No report contents are admitted. Returned receipts are validated locally against the unchanged report and retained request before linking.

external_boundaries.purpose: Bind one local model-data report to a Mparanza server timestamp and Ed25519 signature, then let the studio or its customer verify the retained proof
external_boundaries.retention: Mparanza retains the opaque receipt UUID, server timestamp, Vera version, report digest, signature, signature key ID, and implicit receipt schema version as the proof record, without an automatic deletion period. The local HTML and JSON receipt remain in the studio's run output, or in a supplementary run receipts directory for a retry after output finalization, until the studio removes them. Administrative deletion of the server proof must be requested from Mparanza and makes later verification impossible.

external_boundaries.content: The existing installation capability authenticates closed-schema events: random run and event UUIDs, sequence, catalog pipeline ID, host, observed product version, timestamps, explicit user/synthetic/agent-test classification and started/resumed/completed/failed/cancelled state. Optional links contain only an existing signed receipt UUID/report digest or an owned incident report UUID. Run ownership, single-run receipt binding and the retained signature are checked server-side. The original stamping service does not attest the identity of the author of a report. The service receives no task text, client identity, filenames, source data, prompt or professional output. Existing connection metadata and rate limiting apply. Saved connector identity is not inferred to be a native computer. Native senders also present the existing anonymous native-computer capability and observed native app when available. The server retains the established computer binding; unlinked guests remain unlinked until an actual native proof is received. Connector-owned runs can obtain the bounded per-run proof described above; run-specific computer bindings are used by counts and completion indicators. No personal account information or hardware identifier is collected. The product field is explicit. Product, run owner and receipt product must match. Baselines and function catalogues are distinct per product.
controls: Events are durably queued before transport and acknowledged by exact UUID, owner, sequence and hash. Interruptions stay outcome unknown; repeated submissions are idempotent.
Synthetic and agent-test runs are excluded from user metrics. Studio Archive is infrastructure and cannot be selected as a rated process.
The host AI selects the primary process and observes actual task completion. Counters and hashes do not assert professional correctness or independent model delivery.

The shared implementation binds registrations, OAuth resources, task events, report signatures, feedback and update downloads to one product. Existing unmapped installations and receipt schema 1 remain Vera. Physical-computer identity is shared, while usage catalogues and testing epochs are separated by product.

Authenticated event acknowledgements and run status expose the original owner's proven Computer ID and whether an actual signed receipt is linked. Missing linkage remains explicit and returns bounded follow-up instructions. Neither reporting gap changes the professional outcome or authorizes broader host access.

When local HTTPS is unavailable, the authenticated connector can stamp the exact retained receipt request for an owned run. The allow-list admits only receipt UUID, product/version, schema and report digest. It returns the same signed proof; a separate verified receipt event links it to the original run. No report or source contents are transmitted.

Connector-owned workflow acknowledgements return a random 15-minute proof scoped only to binding that original run to a native computer. The existing native helper adds its private computer capability and observed app. The server stores only the ticket hash, checks product, expiry and app, rejects re-binding, and never replaces the original owner or associates all runs from one saved connection with one computer. The proof cannot authorize other reporting operations. Exact event replay obtains a fresh proof without another event.

Host-link tickets expire after 15 minutes; their hashes and established run-to-computer bindings remain until administrative deletion. The raw short-lived proof is returned only in an authenticated acknowledgement and not in status or operator projections.
